lesson.grammar_point: past continuous versus past simple for interrupted actions

listenings.text: Good morning. This is an announcement for passengers waiting on platform four. We are sorry to tell you that the eight fifteen service is delayed by approximately forty minutes. While the train was leaving the depot this morning, a signal failed on the line just outside the city, and engineers are working on it now. If you were planning to change at the central station, please speak to a member of staff, because your connection is also affected. A replacement bus service is waiting outside the main entrance for passengers who cannot wait. We apologise for the delay and we thank you for your patience this morning.

The strangest thing happened to me last Tuesday. I was driving to a meeting on the other side of the city and I was already twenty minutes late. I was sitting in a traffic jam, going nowhere, when my telephone rang. It was the client. I was about to apologise when he said, do not worry, I am stuck as well, on the same road, about six cars behind you. So we did the whole meeting on the telephone, from two cars in the same traffic jam, and it was the best conversation we had all year. Luckily nobody moved for forty minutes. I have never been so happy about traffic in my life.

extra_audio.text: Rachel asks Janderson why he missed the beginning of the call. He answers that he was on his way to the office when the road closed. Rachel asks him what he did then. He says he was sitting in a traffic jam for fifty minutes and did not move at all. Rachel tells him that she was about to call him when he finally arrived, and he says that luckily he made it before the client did.
